title: A wrapped label says which width you are looking at
goal: When a label is too wide for the box holding it, the app breaks it onto more lines and narrows it to fit. Its width then reads as the room the box had, not as how wide its own words are, and the two numbers look like they disagree with each other. A person building to a spec cannot tell which one they are reading.
notes: Comes out of a-stretched-piece-stops-offering-a-size-you-cann (2026-09-06), which was asked to make this a readout and found the premise false. Evidence, verified with a test: a label with natural width 166 inside a 100-wide free group flows to 104 with wrappedByItsContainer = true. Typing 60 or 140 CLEARS the flag in Layer.resized and sticks; only 400 (wider than the words) snaps back to 104, because textHugsItsWords is then true again and GroupFlow.wrapping re-wraps it. So the W field is a live control, not a decided number, and it must NOT become a GeometryReadout: that would remove the keyboard way to set a paragraph width while the canvas drag keeps it. The real complaint is the audit line 2026-09-05-words-that-wrap rough3: two numbers that look like they disagree. Likely answers are a word in the Layout section rather than a change to the W field. Ask the user before building: this is a visual-direction call.
acceptance: The width shown for a label the container wrapped is unambiguous: it is clear whether it is the room the container gave it or how wide the words themselves are
Typing a width into a wrapped label still works exactly as it does today, because it does work: anything at or below the words own width sticks and makes it a paragraph, the same as dragging its edge
A label nothing has wrapped is unchanged
A screenshot in the audit shows a wrapped label beside its number

log.note: Adversarial review before building: reproduced the complaint rather than trusting it, and found the premise is TRUE but mis-stated. Core repro (throwaway test): a label whose words are 141 wide, inside a free group with Largest width 100, comes out with a frame of 100 while the WRAPPED words only reach 78. Same for two other phrases (104 natural, 100 box, 63 ink; 151 natural, 100 box, 89 ink). textWrapped(inRoom:) sets the frame to the whole room the container allowed, not to the longest line the wrap produced.

Reproduced live in the probe app too, with Screen Recording granted. Scripts/playtest/wrapped-label-width-walk.json builds the audit's own example: a square and the words Save all the changes, stacked, Largest width 140, then picks the LABEL. Capture wrapped-2-label-sc.png: the label's selection outline runs the full 140 while the longest line stops about 29 short of it, and W reads 140. So the two numbers that look like they disagree are the label's W and the words a person can see.

Checked the ripple before proposing a change: GroupFlow.placed decides the group's width from the UNWRAPPED children, then wraps, then only re-measures height. Verified: a group with Largest 100 holding a label whose wrapped ink is 78 comes out 100. So narrowing the label to its words does not on its own narrow the group; a group that hugs would stay at its ceiling with a visible gap unless it is re-measured after the wrap too. That is the part a person should decide, so it went into the decision rather than being guessed.

Shortest version considered and rejected: turning W into a readout. The predecessor task already proved that removes the only keyboard way to set a paragraph width while the canvas drag keeps it. Stretched and filled labels are untouched either way, since GroupFlow.wrapRooms excludes them and they keep going through sizeIsDecidedByItsContainer.

Waiting on a visual-direction decision: after a wrap, should a label be as wide as the words that came out, or as wide as the room it was given? Reproduced both in a test and live in the probe app, with a capture in the brief.
